To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

functional searchlight analysis can reveal distributed neural coding in the human cerebral cortex, and that functional searchlights are more accurate than anatomical searchlights in decoding brain representations of visual features, auditory features, and semantic features.

functional searchlight analysis, which groups voxels based on functional similarity and ignores anatomical proximity, reveals that the human brain represents visual, auditory, semantic, and object information more widely distributed across brain regions than previously acknowledged and can improve model-based decoding accuracy.

(1) functional searchlight reveals that visual, auditory, semantic, and object representations are more widely distributed throughout the brain than previously thought; (2) functional searchlight improves model-based similarity and classification accuracy; and (3) functional searchlight provides a new way of evaluating and constraining computational models with brain activation.
